decisions.reason: The corrected U3 supply wiring and D+/D- pass-through implement the separate ESD-protection Requirement without changing the native USB interface's required data lines, programming role, enumeration modes, or orientation support.
The source changes USBLC6 wiring downstream of the connector and does not change the selected USB-C connector, its data-line support, compatibility, or availability constraints.
Separating U3 pin 5 and pin 2 and routing USB data through U3 does not change the standalone 3.3V regulator, source-selection behavior, powered rail, or its unresolved current-rating question.
References to pins 2 and 5 in the source concern the USBLC6 device U3, not the numbered pins or D+/D- assignments of the interboard connectors.
The USB ESD-device wiring decision has no effect on the SPS30 connector, 5V supply, I2C signals, SEL connection, or ground connection.
The source concerns USBLC6 power pins and USB D+/D- routing, not the addressable LEDs' supply, data GPIO, level shifting, or power control.
The USB ESD correction does not change the e-paper backlight's supply selection, PWM control, switching circuit, or population choices.
The source's pass-through language applies to USB D+/D- through U3 and does not affect I2C pull-ups, series resistors, topology, speed, or cable assumptions.
The U3 pin connections are unrelated to the panel-mounted button connector and its PWRON signal tap.
Correcting USBLC6 wiring does not change the requested AXP2101 PWROK test-pad access or signal-trace-only connection.
The source preserves USB data-line ESD protection and does not alter battery overcharge, overdischarge, short-circuit, or DW01A protection behavior.
The USBLC6 symbol and routing correction has no effect on the battery NTC terminal, connector, monitoring function, or controller.
